blocks.text:
قفا نبك من ذِكرى حبيب ومنزل
بسِقطِ اللِّوى بينَ الدَّخول فحَوْملِ

فتوضح فالمقراة لم يَعفُ رسمهاَ
لما نسجتْها من جَنُوب وشمالِ

ترى بَعَرَ الأرْآمِ في عَرَصاتِها
وقيعانها كأنه حبَّ فلفل

كأني غَداةَ البَيْنِ يَوْمَ تَحَمَلّوا
لدى سَمُراتِ الحَيّ ناقِفُ حنظلِ

وُقوفاً بها صَحْبي عَليَّ مَطِيَّهُمْ
يقُولون لا تهلكْ أسىً وتجمّل

وإنَّ شفائي عبرةٌ مهراقةٌ
فهلْ عند رَسمٍ دارِسٍ من مُعوَّلِ

كدأبكَ من أمِّ الحويَرثِ قبلها
وجارتها أمَّ الربابِ بمأسل

فَفاضَت دُموعُ العَينِ مِنّي صَبابَةً
عَلى النَحرِ حَتّى بَلَّ دَمعِيَ مِحمَلي

ألا ربَّ يومٍ لك مِنْهُنَّ صالح
ولا سيّما يومٍ بدارَةِ جُلْجُلِ

ويوم عقرتُ للعذارى مطيتي
فيا عَجَباً من كورِها المُتَحَمَّلِ

فظلَّ العذارى يرتمينَ بلحمها
وشحمٍ كهداب الدمقس المفتل

ويوم دخلتُ الخدرِ خدر عنيزة
فقالت لك الويلات إنكَ مُرجلي

تقولُ وقد مالَ الغَبيطُ بنا معاً
عقرت بعيري يا امرأ القيس فانزلِ

فقُلتُ لها سيري وأرْخي زِمامَهُ
ولا تُبعديني من جناك المعللِ

فمِثلِكِ حُبْلى قد طَرَقْتُ ومُرْضعٍ
فألهيتُها عن ذي تمائمَ محول

إذا ما بكى من خلفها انْصَرَفَتْ لهُ
بشِقٍّ وَتحتي شِقُّها لم يُحَوَّلِ

ويوماً على ظهر الكثيبِ تعذَّرت
عَليّ وَآلَتْ حَلْفَةً لم تَحَلَّلِ

أفاطِمُ مهلاً بعض هذا التدلل
وإن كنتِ قد أزمعت صرمي فأجملي

وَإنْ تكُ قد ساءتكِ مني خَليقَةٌ
فسُلّي ثيابي من ثيابِكِ تَنْسُلِ

أغَرّكِ مني أنّ حُبّكِ قاتِلي
وأنكِ مهما تأمري القلب يفعل

ومَا ذَرَفَتْ عَيْناكِ إلا لتَضْرِبي
بسَهمَيكِ في أعشارِ قَلبٍ مُقَتَّلِ

و بيضةِ خدر لا يرامُ خباؤها
تَمَتّعتُ من لَهْوٍ بها غيرَ مُعجَلِ

تجاوزْتُ أحْراساً إلَيها ومَعْشَراً
عليّ حِراساً لو يُسروّن مقتلي

إذا ما الثريا في السماء تعرضت
تعرضَ أثناء الوشاح المفصَّلِ

فجِئْتُ وقد نَضَّتْ لنَوْمٍ ثيابَها
لدى السِّترِ إلاَّ لِبْسَةَ المُتَفَضِّلِ

فقالت يمين الله ما لكَ حيلةٌ
وما إن أرى عنك الغوايةَ تنجلي

خَرَجْتُ بها أمشي تَجُرّ وَراءَنا
على أثَرَيْنا ذَيْلَ مِرْطٍ مُرَحَّلِ

فلما أجزْنا ساحة الحيِّ وانتحى
بنا بطنُ خَبْتٍ ذي حِقافٍ عَقَنْقَلِ

هصرتُ بِفودي رأسها فتمايلت
عليَّ هضيمَ الكَشحِ رِيّا المُخَلخَلِ

إِذا اِلتَفَتَت نَحوي تَضَوَّعَ ريحُها
نَسيمَ الصَبا جاءَت بِرَيّا القَرَنفُلِ

مُهَفْهَفَةٌ بَيْضاءُ غيرُ مُفاضَةٍ
ترائبها مصقولةٌ كالسجنجل

كِبِكْرِ المُقاناةِ البَياضِ بصُفْرَةٍ
غذاها نميرُ الماء غير المحللِِ

تصد وتبدي عن أسيلٍ وتتَّقي
بناظرَةٍ من وَحش وَجْرَةَ مُطفِلِ

وجيد كجيد الرئم ليس بفاحِش
إذا هيَ نَصّتْهُ وَلا بمُعَطَّلِ

وَفَرعٍ يَزينُ المَتنَ أَسوَدَ فاحِمٍ
أَثيثٍ كَقِنوِ النَخلَةِ المُتَعَثكِلِ

غَدائِرُها مُستَشزِراتٌ إِلى العُلا
تَضِلُّ العِقاصَ في مُثَنّىً وَمُرسَلِ

وكشح لطيف كالجديل مخصر
وساق كأنبوبِ السقي المُذلل

وَتَعْطو برخَصٍ غيرِ شَثْنٍ كأنّهُ
أساريعُ ظبي أو مساويكُ إسحلِ

تُضيء الظلامَ بالعشاء كأنها
منارةُ ممسى راهب متبتل

وَتُضْحي فَتِيتُ المِسكِ فوق فراشها
نؤومُ الضُّحى لم تَنْتَطِقْ عن تَفضُّلِ

إلى مثلها يرنو الحليمُ صبابة
إذا ما اسبكَرّتْ بينَ درْعٍ ومِجْوَلِ

تَسَلَّت عِماياتُ الرِجالِ عَنِ الصِبا
وَلَيسَ فُؤادي عَن هَواكِ بِمُنسَلِ

ألا رُبّ خَصْمٍ فيكِ ألْوَى رَدَدتُه
نصيح على تعذَاله غير مؤتل

وليل كموج البحر أرخى سدولهُ
عليَّ بأنواع الهموم ليبتلي

فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لما تَمَطّى بصلبه
وأردَف أعجازاً وناءَ بكلْكلِ

ألا أيّها اللّيلُ الطّويلُ ألا انْجَلي
بصُبْحٍ وما الإصْباحَ مِنك بأمثَلِ

فيا لكَ من ليلْ كأنَّ نجومهُ
بكل مغار الفتل شدت بيذبلِ

كأن الثريا علِّقت في مصامها
بأمْراسِ كتّانٍ إلى صُمّ جَندَلِ

وَقَد أَغتَدي وَالطَيرُ في وُكُناتِها
بِمُنجَرِدٍ قَيدِ الأَوابِدِ هَيكَلِ

مِكَرٍّ مِفَرٍّ مُقبِلٍ مُدبِرٍ مَعاً
كَجُلمودِ صَخرٍ حَطَّهُ السَيلُ مِن عَلِ

كُمَيتٍ يَزِلُّ اللِبدُ عَن حالِ مَتنِهِ
كَما زَلَّتِ الصَفواءُ بِالمُتَنَزَّلِ

مسحٍّ إذا ما السابحاتُ على الونى
أثرنَ غباراً بالكديد المركل

على العقبِ جيَّاش كأن اهتزامهُ
إذا جاش فيه حميُه غَليُ مِرْجلِ

يطيرُ الغلامُ الخفُّ على صهواته
وَيُلْوي بأثْوابِ العَنيفِ المُثقَّلِ

دَريرٍ كَخُذْروفِ الوَليدِ أمَرّهُ
تقلبُ كفيهِ بخيطٍ مُوصلِ

لهُ أيطلا ظبيٍ وساقا نعامة
وإرخاء سرحانٍ وتقريبُ تنفلِ

كأن على الكتفين منه إذا انتحى
مَداكَ عَروسٍ أوْ صَلايةَ حنظلِ

وباتَ عَلَيْهِ سَرْجُهُ وَلجامُهُ
وباتَ بعيني قائماً غير مرسل

فعنَّ لنا سربٌ كأنَّ نعاجَه
عَذارَى دَوارٍ في مُلاءٍ مُذَيَّلِ

فأدبرنَ كالجزع المفصل بينه
بجيدِ مُعَمٍّ في العَشيرَةِ مُخْوَلِ

فألحَقَنا بالهادِياتِ وَدُونَهُ
جواحِرها في صرةٍ لم تزيَّل

فَعادى عِداءً بَينَ ثَوْرٍ وَنَعْجَةٍ
دِراكاً ولم يَنْضَحْ بماءٍ فيُغسَلِ

وظلّ طُهاةُ اللّحمِ من بينِ مُنْضِجٍ
صَفيفَ شِواءٍ أوْ قَديرٍ مُعَجَّلِ

ورُحنا راحَ الطرفُ ينفض رأسه
متى ما تَرَقَّ العينُ فيه تَسَفَّلِ

كأنَّ دماءَ الهادياتِ بنحره
عُصارةُ حِنّاءٍ بشَيْبٍ مُرْجّلِ

وأنتَ إذا استدبرتُه سدَّ فرجه
بضاف فويق الأرض ليس بأعزل

أحار ترى برقاً أريك وميضه
كلمع اليدينِ في حبي مُكلل

يُضيءُ سَناهُ أوْ مَصَابيحُ راهِبٍ
أهان السليط في الذَّبال المفتَّل

قعدت له وصحيبتي بين حامر
وبين اكام بعدم متأمل

وأضحى يسحُّ الماء عن كل فيقة
يكبُّ على الأذقان دوحَ الكنهبل

وتيماءَ لم يترُك بها جِذع نخلة
وَلا أُطُماً إلا مَشيداً بجَنْدَلِ

كأن ذرى رأس المجيمر غدوةً
من السَّيلِ وَالأغْثاء فَلكةُ مِغزَلِ

كأنَّ أباناً في أفانينِ ودقهِ
كَبيرُ أُناسٍ في بِجادٍ مُزَمَّلِ

وَألْقى بصَحْراءِ الغَبيطِ بَعاعَهُ
نزول اليماني ذي العياب المخوَّل

كَأَنَّ سِباعاً فيهِ غَرقى غُدَيَّةً
بِأَرجائِهِ القُصوى أَنابيشُ عَنصُلِ

على قَطَنٍ بالشَّيْمِ أيْمَنُ صَوْبهِ
وَأيْسَرُهُ عَلى السّتارِ فَيَذْبُلِ

وَأَلقى بِبَيسانَ مَعَ اللَيلِ بَركَهُ
فَأَنزَلَ مِنهُ العَصمَ مِن كُلِّ مَنزِلِ

english.text:
Stop, you two: let us weep at the memory of a beloved and a dwelling,
at the edge of the winding sands between al-Dakhul and Hawmal.

And Tudih and al-Miqrat: its traces have not vanished,
for south wind and north wind have woven over them.

You see the droppings of white antelope in its courtyards
and low places, like scattered peppercorns.

On the morning of separation, when they loaded up to leave,
I stood by the tribe's acacias like one splitting bitter colocynth.

My companions halted their mounts beside me there,
saying, 'Do not destroy yourself with grief; bear it well.'

My cure is tears poured out;
but is there any solace at an effaced encampment?

It is as you were with Umm al-Huwayrith before her,
and her neighbor Umm al-Rabab at Ma'sal.

My eyes overflowed with tears of longing
onto my chest, until my tears soaked my sword-belt.

How many happy days you had with them,
especially that day at Darat Juljul!

The day I slaughtered my riding camel for the maidens:
how strange the burden of her gear as they carried it!

The maidens kept tossing portions of her flesh to one another,
and fat like the fringes of tightly woven silk.

And the day I entered the curtained litter of Unayza;
she said, 'Woe to you! You will make me walk!'

As the litter tilted under us both, she said,
'You have crippled my camel, Imru al-Qays. Get down!'

I told her, 'Go on, and let his rein hang loose;
do not keep me from the fruit you offer again and again.'

Many a pregnant woman like you, and many a nursing mother, I visited by night,
distracting her from her amulet-wearing year-old child.

When he cried behind her, she turned toward him
with one side, while the side beneath me did not move.

One day upon the sand dune she resisted me
and swore an oath she would not release herself from.

Fatima, gently: enough of this disdain!
If you have resolved to break with me, do it graciously.

If some trait of mine has offended you,
draw my clothes from yours, and they will slip away.

Has it made you bold that your love is killing me,
and that my heart will do whatever you command?

Your eyes shed tears only to strike
with their two arrows the shattered pieces of my stricken heart.

Many a secluded beauty, her tent beyond approach,
I have enjoyed at leisure, without being hurried away.

I passed guards to reach her, and a company
eager for my death, if only they could conceal it.

When the Pleiades stretched across the sky
like the jeweled folds of a woman's sash,

I came to her when she had taken off her clothes for sleep
behind the curtain, keeping only a loose house garment.

She said, 'By God, there is no dealing with you!
I see that your waywardness will never leave you.'

I led her out on foot; behind us she dragged
the hem of her figured mantle over our two trails.

When we had passed beyond the camp's open ground,
and a hollow among tangled sand ridges sheltered us,

I drew her toward me by the locks beside her head; she leaned against me,
slender at the waist, full where the anklets rested.

When she turned toward me, her fragrance spread
like the east wind carrying the scent of cloves.

Slender and fair, with no heaviness of body,
her breastbone shone polished as a mirror.

Like a first ostrich egg, its white mingled with yellow,
nourished by pure water that no crowd has troubled.

She turns away, then shows a smooth cheek, guarding herself
with the gaze of a wild doe of Wajra that has a fawn.

Her neck is like an antelope's, not overlong
when she raises it, nor bare of ornaments.

Coal-black hair adorns her back,
thick as the clustered fruit of a laden palm.

Its braids are lifted upward;
the tied locks lose themselves among twisted and loosened strands.

A delicate waist, slender as a twisted rein,
and a leg like the stem of a well-watered, tended palm.

She reaches with soft fingers, not coarse ones,
like the small worms of Zaby or tooth-sticks cut from the ishl tree.

At evening she lights the darkness, as though she were
the lamp at the night retreat of a solitary monk.

Morning finds crumbled musk upon her bed;
she sleeps late, without girding herself for work over her loose garment.

Even a sober man gazes longingly at one like her
when she stands tall between gown and light robe.

Other men's blind passions have found relief from youthful love,
but my heart has not slipped free of loving you.

How many stubborn opponents I have turned back over you,
sincere advisers who spared no effort in their reproaches!

Many a night, like the waves of the sea, let down its curtains
upon me with every kind of care, to put me to the test.

I said to it, as it stretched its spine,
dragged its hindquarters after it, and pressed down its chest:

'Long night, will you not clear away
with morning? Yet morning is no better than you.'

What a night you are! Its stars seem tied
to Mount Yadhbul with every tightly twisted rope.

As though the Pleiades were hung fast in their places
by ropes of flax bound to solid rock.

Often I set out early, while birds were still in their nests,
on a great, sleek horse that holds wild game captive.

Charging, retreating, advancing, wheeling, all at once,
like a boulder swept down from a height by a flood.

A dark bay: the saddle-felt slips from his smooth back
as a polished stone slips beneath one descending it.

He pours onward when other swift horses, weary,
raise dust from the hard ground their hooves have beaten.

Even after running he surges with strength; his snorting,
when his heat rises, is like the boiling of a cauldron.

He throws the light boy from his back
and sends the clothes of the heavy, rough rider flying.

Unflagging, like a child's spinning toy
set whirling by the turns of his hands on a joined string.

He has the flanks of an antelope, the legs of an ostrich,
the easy stride of a wolf, and the short gallop of a young fox.

Across his shoulders, when he turns, it is as though there lay
a bride's grinding stone or a slab for crushing colocynth.

He spent the night with saddle and bridle upon him;
he stood before my eyes, not turned loose.

A herd appeared before us; its cows were like
maidens circling Duwar in long, trailing robes.

They turned away like onyx beads strung with other gems
around the neck of one richly endowed with paternal and maternal kin.

He brought us up to the leaders while behind them
the stragglers remained in a close, unbroken cluster.

He overtook a bull and a cow in a single pursuit,
and did not break into sweat that needed washing off.

The cooks stayed at their meat: some roasting
sliced flesh, others hastily boiling it in a pot.

We returned, and the noble horse came back tossing his head;
whenever the eye climbed over his beauty, it was drawn downward again.

The blood of the leading beasts upon his chest
was like the juice of henna upon combed gray hair.

Seen from behind, the space between his legs was filled
by a full tail just above the ground, never swept to one side.

Harith, do you see that lightning whose flash I show you,
like the flicker of hands in a bank of crowned clouds?

Its brightness shines like the lamps of a monk
who has poured oil freely upon their twisted wicks.

My companions and I sat watching it between Hamir
and Akam, far from the storm we observed.

By morning it poured water from every swollen cloud,
throwing the great kanahbal trees face down.

At Tayma it left no palm trunk standing,
nor fortress, except one built firmly of stone.

At dawn the summit of al-Mujaymir, encircled
by floodwater and debris, looked like a spindle-whorl.

Aban, amid the varied streams of its downpour,
was like a great chief wrapped in a striped cloak.

It cast its heavy rain upon the plain of al-Ghabit,
like a well-equipped Yemeni merchant unloading his packs.

At dawn the drowned wild beasts in its farthest reaches
looked like uprooted bulbs of wild onion.

As we watched, the right edge of its rain lay over Qatan,
and its left over al-Sitar and Yadhbul.

At night it laid its heavy breast upon Baysan,
and drove the white-marked mountain goats from every refuge.
